title: M1: Implement a bounded, server-side teaching AI adapter
body:
Connect one real model through a server-side adapter for the sample chapter.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Keys remain server-side.
- [ ] Book and teaching configuration are versioned.
- [ ] Explanation, role-play and feedback modes are explicit.
- [ ] Sessions have bounded input, time and usage.
- [ ] Errors, cancellation and unconfigured state are clear.
- [ ] Demonstration and real AI are visibly distinguished.

See docs/PRD.md and docs/TEACHING_SPEC.md.

title: M1: Build an evaluation set for the first learning unit
body:
Create unfamiliar cases and a feedback rubric for distinguishing facts, interpretations and useful questions.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Include common mistakes and reasonable alternative responses.
- [ ] Separate development and comparison cases.
- [ ] Check consistency and unsupported judgments.
- [ ] Include an independent transfer task.
- [ ] Report learning results only after a real evaluation.

title: M1: Refine the responsive reading and practice experience
body:
Test the actual interface on phone and desktop sizes, including keyboard and assistive labels.

Acceptance:
- [ ] No clipped reading, navigation or controls.
- [ ] Long answers remain readable.
- [ ] Retry and session reset behave consistently.
- [ ] Local-save failures preserve the current draft.
- [ ] Record the tested viewports and remaining limitations.

title: M2: Add identity and durable user-owned learning records
body:
Design authentication and persistent storage before enabling multi-user publishing.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Progress and drafts survive another session/device.
- [ ] Users can access only their own private records.
- [ ] Creator-facing feedback is intentionally scoped.
- [ ] Migrate or export browser-local data.
- [ ] Test unauthorized access and failed saves.

title: M2: Create a guided book editor and versioned publishing flow
body:
Help creators describe audience, objectives, reading, practices and feedback without coding prompts.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Validate the book package.
- [ ] Support preview and self-testing.
- [ ] Separate draft, review and published states.
- [ ] Keep published versions reproducible.
- [ ] Test with a creator who did not build the platform.

title: M3: Meter real usage and validate unit economics
body:
Record actual authoring and learning-service consumption before selling credits.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Separate authoring, text practice and voice consumption.
- [ ] Handle retries and failed/cancelled requests.
- [ ] Show understandable estimates and limits.
- [ ] Keep measured costs separate from assumptions.
- [ ] No fabricated cash balance or learning tokens.

title: M3: Design payments, internal credits and creator settlement
body:
Implement only after authentication, a durable ledger, and real usage measurements exist.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Define purchase, reserve, debit, reversal and refund behavior.
- [ ] Use idempotent financial operations.
- [ ] Separate content income and service costs.
- [ ] Document creator payout terms and evidence.
- [ ] Keep reputation and learning scores separate from spendable balances.

No tradable-token issuance is included.

title: Community: Add an English introduction and contributor walkthrough
body:
Help international software and teaching contributors try the prototype and choose a small task.

Acceptance:
- [ ] Explain the real current capabilities.
- [ ] Walk through the sample chapter and creator flow.
- [ ] Include one teaching and one code contribution example.
- [ ] Preserve the Chinese-first reader experience.
